result.title: ADAPT: Adaptive Decision and Abstention with Pool-Size-Aware Thresholds for Service Routing
result.summary: Retrieval-based classifiers efficiently route queries to specialised services, but they typically select a candidate even when no suitable service exists. We introduce Adaptive Decision and Abstention with Pool-Size-Aware Thresholds for Service Routing (ADAPT), a lightweight routing architecture with an explicit fallback option that enables queries to abstain from specialist selection. ADAPT uses the separation between the highest relevance score and the candidate score distribution as routing confidence. Experiments across retrieval models and increasing numbers of services reveal a consistent empirical behaviour: the confidence distribution changes systematically with candidate-pool size K, making fixed abstention thresholds increasingly miscalibrated. ADAPT addresses this effect with a K-aware threshold that adapts as services are added without classifier retraining. Evaluation across two specialist datasets shows that this simple mechanism provides an effective accuracy-cost trade-off compared with generative LLM routing, supporting lightweight and dynamically extensible service-routing architectures.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ADAPT，一种带显式弃权（fallback）选项的轻量服务路由架构：以最高相关度分数与候选分数分布的差距作为路由置信度，并用随候选池大小 K 自适应、无需重训分类器的阈值来纠正固定阈值随 K 增大而失准的问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「分数分布差距作为置信度 + 依候选规模自适应阈值」的弃权机制，可能为 LVR 中的 STOP 决策与停止阈值标定（何时证据已足够、何时弃权）提供可供核查的概念线索，但该置信度定义能否迁移到 latent 推理状态尚不清楚。
